decisions.reason: The candidate still constrains the bowls to a compact, not overly large enclosure, while the client now accepts the bulkier enclosure required by the internal solenoid and piping. The bowl-capacity preferences remain unchanged.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Larry, 

I’m fine with the on/off buttons being placed where they are. I’m also fine with it being bulkier. 

I’ll work on a new logo this weekend. I don’t dislike the logo, just want to see if I can come up with something better.

decisions.reason: Acceptance of a bulkier enclosure does not change the required 12-ounce cup clearance or the specified clearance height.
The platform remains required beneath the mixer and its edge-to-edge alignment is relational, so it remains valid even if the enclosure is bulkier.
The source changes the accepted enclosure size, not the requirement for a stable, vibration-resistant base.
The enclosure bulk is attributed to the solenoid and piping, but the source does not change the spout location, orientation, fabrication style, or pour direction.
The client accepts the bulkier enclosure but does not change any beige, green, platform, or button color requirement.
Accepting a bulkier enclosure does not remove or modify the DJ-turntable visual theme.
The source addresses enclosure bulk and button placement, not splash behavior or splash-control methods.
The source accepts the physical consequence of the already selected solenoid and piping but does not change the V1 component-selection or custom-spout strategy.
Enclosure bulk does not change the selected whisk head, bowl compatibility, or whisk-positioning criterion.
The source does not change the wall-power architecture, supply capacity, controllers, or electrical load requirements.
The accepted additional enclosure bulk accommodates dispensing hardware but does not change the required smooth, controlled, froth-preserving flow.
